I'm an economist with the Government of Saskatchewan's Ministry of Finance. At work I build the tools that show how the provincial economy is doing and what a shock to it would cost: impact models for things like US tariffs, and the data products behind our monthly monitoring.

Outside work, I write about the Canadian economy and publish the data and methods with each piece. This site is where those notebooks live. The idea is simple: if I show you a chart, you should be able to rebuild it, either in Python or in Excel.

I grew up in Ghana. I hold an MA in Economics from the University of Saskatchewan and a BA in Economics and Mathematics from the University of Ghana.

If you work on economic measurement, or you've rebuilt one of my notebooks and want to compare methods, I'd like to hear from you.

*Everything on this site is my own work and my own views. It doesn't represent the Government of Saskatchewan.*
